newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek official sees Athens bourse trade Monday.
newsitem.headline: Greek official sees Athens bourse trade Monday.

text.p: A senior national economy ministry official said he expected the Athens bourse to operate normally on Monday and said the settlement problem which shut down the exchange on Friday would be cleared up over the weekend.
In response to questions, Antonis Fotiadis, general secretary of the national economy ministry, told reporters talks with brokers would continue at the weekend to sort out problems.
But brokers boycotting the exchange said they were considering the matter and that no decision had been taken on whether to resume trading on Monday.
Several brokers said Fotiadis had done little to resolve the underlying problem and predicted there would be disagreement among the brokers as to whether to resume trading on Monday.
Fotiadis told reporters Athens bourse member Delta Securities was in the red with the clearing house for 2.6 billion drachmas, more than the 1.2 billion initially reported in the media.
Delta was again unable to meet its settlement obligations on Friday as the Athens bourse halted trade after a boycott vote by member brokerages.
Any shareholder losses from Delta Securities' settlement problem would be covered by the exchange's guarantee fund, Fotiadis said after meeting shareholder representatives.
He made clear that the state would not pick up the tab nor guarantee any future losses arising from settlement incidents.
The national economy ministry would consider legislative measures aimed at improving the operating mechanisms of the stock exchange and discourage regulatory violations.
